interface: rebrew.near_diag.analyze; no relocation masking; independently materialized candidate references

alternate-mov-encoding.suggestion: Every differing byte is the same instruction re-encoded with a different opcode form — semantically identical, but NOT byte-identical.  Byte-identity needs the original compiler version's encodings, or 'rebrew prove' for PROVEN equivalence.

different-return-constant.suggestion: Instruction selection differs — try alternative C constructs (e.g. pointer arithmetic vs indexing, cast-based masking).

different-return-register.suggestion: Every differing byte is a register-allocation difference — the same instructions, different registers.  reccmp counts this as a 100% effective match, but it is NOT byte-identical: 'rebrew prove' can establish semantic equivalence (PROVEN), or try register-nudging C tweaks (reorder expressions, swap loop counters) if byte-identity is required.

changed-immediate.suggestion: Control flow / block layout differs — try restructuring loops or if/else; may need a compiler-pattern workaround.

changed-call-target.suggestion: Control flow / block layout differs — try restructuring loops or if/else; may need a compiler-pattern workaround.

stack-slot.suggestion: Control flow / block layout differs — try restructuring loops or if/else; may need a compiler-pattern workaround.

same-call-shifted.suggestion: Every differing byte is the same instruction re-encoded with a different opcode form — semantically identical, but NOT byte-identical.  Byte-identity needs the original compiler version's encodings, or 'rebrew prove' for PROVEN equivalence.

hints: local layout differs — /O1 vs /O2, a missing/extra local, or a /Gs stack probe; compare the [ebp±N] slots below

stack_frame.caveat: Diagnostic only: prologue allocation includes compiler temporaries and stack-slot coloring; its delta does not imply missing source locals byte-for-byte.
